pharm: Binds selectively to the omega-1 (alpha-1 subunit) site of the GABA-A/benzodiazepine receptor complex, enhancing GABA-mediated inhibition to produce sedation and decrease sleep latency
tags: Schedule IV / habit forming / boxed warning

Mild-moderate: reduce to 5 mg; not recommended in severe hepatic impairment

summary: Zaleplon is a non-benzodiazepine (pyrazolopyrimidine) sedative-hypnotic indicated for the short-term treatment of insomnia, where it shortens the time to sleep onset. It acts at the GABA-A/benzodiazepine receptor complex with preferential binding to the omega-1 receptor. It has a rapid onset and very short half-life (~1 hour) and must be taken immediately before bed. It carries a boxed warning for complex sleep behaviors and is a Schedule IV controlled substance that can cause dependence.
indications: Short-term treatment of insomnia (shown to decrease time to sleep onset for up to 30 days)

dosage.d: 10 mg orally immediately before bedtime; 5 mg may suffice for certain low-weight individuals
dosage.n: 20 mg may be considered for occasional patients not benefiting from a lower dose; doses >20 mg not recommended
More sensitive to hypnotics; doses over 10 mg not recommended
Reduced clearance; not recommended in severe hepatic impairment

admin: Take orally immediately before bedtime, or after going to bed and having difficulty falling asleep
Only take when able to devote a full night (at least 4 hours) to sleep before being active again
Do not take with or immediately after a heavy, high-fat meal (slows absorption and reduces effect on sleep latency)
Do not take with alcohol or other CNS depressants
Use for the shortest duration; reassess if insomnia persists beyond 7-10 days
moa: Zaleplon is a hypnotic with a chemical structure unrelated to benzodiazepines or barbiturates that interacts with the GABA-benzodiazepine (GABA-BZ) receptor complex. It binds selectively to the brain omega-1 receptor situated on the alpha subunit of the GABA-A/chloride ion channel receptor complex and potentiates TBPS binding, with preferential (high) affinity for the omega-1 over the omega-2 receptor. Modulation of the chloride channel macromolecular complex is thought to mediate its sedative effects.

Hypersensitivity to zaleplon or any excipient in the formulation

Depression (worsening or suicidal ideation may emerge)
monitor: Complex sleep behaviors and next-day impairment
Signs of abuse, dependence, or worsening depression

preg: There are no adequate and well-controlled studies of zaleplon in pregnant women. It should be used during pregnancy only if clearly needed; sedative-hypnotic use late in pregnancy may produce neonatal CNS depression. Advise pregnant patients of the potential risks to the fetus.
lact: A small amount of zaleplon is excreted in human breast milk, with the highest amount about 1 hour after a dose. Because this may result in potentially important concentrations in infants and the effects on a nursing infant are not known, it is recommended that nursing mothers not take zaleplon.
renal: No dosage adjustment is necessary in patients with mild to moderate renal impairment. Zaleplon has not been adequately studied in patients with severe renal impairment.
hepatic: In patients with mild to moderate hepatic insufficiency, reduce the dose to 5 mg because of reduced clearance. Zaleplon is not recommended in patients with severe hepatic impairment.

major: Alcohol - potentiates CNS-impairing effects (balance, reaction time, psychomotor performance)
Other CNS depressants (benzodiazepines, opioids, tricyclic antidepressants, antipsychotics) - additive CNS and respiratory depression
Imipramine, thioridazine - additive decreased alertness and impaired psychomotor performance
moderate: Cimetidine - inhibits aldehyde oxidase and CYP3A4, increases zaleplon levels (consider lower starting dose)
Rifampin and other strong CYP3A4 inducers - decrease zaleplon plasma levels and efficacy
minor: Paroxetine - no pharmacokinetic interaction (CYP2D6 not involved)

interactions.alcohol: Avoid - additive CNS depression and impairment
interactions.diagnostics: No specific laboratory test interference described

counsel: Take only right before bed and only when you can stay in bed for a full night
This medicine can be habit forming - take exactly as prescribed, do not increase the dose, and use short-term only
Do not drink alcohol or take other sedating medicines with it
You may do activities like walking, eating, driving, or calling while not fully awake and not remember them - stop the medicine and tell your clinician if this happens
Avoid a heavy, high-fat meal at the same time, and do not drive or operate machinery until you know how it affects you the next day
pk: Rapid; peak plasma concentration about 1 hour after oral dose
Short; does not accumulate with once-daily dosing; bioavailability ~30% due to presystemic metabolism (aldehyde oxidase, CYP3A4)
Store at 20-25 C (68-77 F); dispense in a light-resistant container
pearls: Habit forming: Yes - zaleplon is a Schedule IV (C-IV) controlled substance with potential for abuse and dependence
Boxed warning: complex sleep behaviors (sleep-walking, sleep-driving) can cause serious injury or death - discontinue immediately if they occur
Ultra-short half-life (~1 hour) targets sleep-onset insomnia and minimizes next-day hangover; can even be dosed in the middle of the night if >=4 hours remain in bed
Avoid high-fat meals (delay absorption) and alcohol/other CNS depressants (additive impairment)
Reduce to 5 mg in the elderly/debilitated and in mild-moderate hepatic impairment; avoid in severe hepatic impairment
missed: Zaleplon is taken only as needed at bedtime; there is no fixed daytime schedule, so a missed dose is simply not taken. Do not take it during the day or unless you can devote at least 4 hours to sleep, and never take an extra or double dose.
overdose: Overdose manifests as varying degrees of CNS depression from drowsiness, mental confusion, and lethargy to ataxia, hypotonia, hypotension, respiratory depression, and rarely coma or, very rarely, death (most fatal outcomes involve concomitant CNS depressants). Treatment is general symptomatic and supportive care with immediate gastric lavage where appropriate and IV fluids as needed; flumazenil may be a useful antagonist. Monitor respiration, pulse, and blood pressure; hemodialysis is unlikely to be useful given high protein binding.
